chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife, or by mutual agreement (khula'), or she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, is it for him to marry her sister? He said: When her bond of marriage is freed and there is no reversion (raj'ah) for him upon her, then for him is that he proposes to her sister.

He said: And he was asked about a man who had two slave-sisters, so he slept with one of them, then slept with the other. He said: When he sleeps with the other, the first becomes prohibited to him until the other dies. I said: What is your view if he sells her, would the first be permissible for him? He said: If he sells her due to a need and no thought of the other crosses his heart, then I do not see a problem with that; and if he sells her only to return to the first, then no, and no prestige.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Reversion (the right to take back a wife during the waiting period without a new contract)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a man to marry two sisters who are either free or slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the conditions for 'jam' al-sitrayn' (gathering two sisters), distinguishing between free women and slave-sisters. For free women, an irrevocable divorce (where no 'raj'a' remains) permits marrying the sister, while for slave-sisters, the prohibition persists until the second sister dies or is sold, with the validity of sale depending on whether it is for genuine need or merely a pretext to reunite with the first.
